messages:
mike: ran a quick nsys capture on the failing 8GPU job, timeline attached (nsys export). seeing repeated 10-20ms hostcopy spikes that line up with gpu kernels stalling
sara: can you paste the nsys waterfall screenshot or flame view?
mike: pasted snippet below (trimmed):
```
Stream 0: kernel A (kv_prefetch) 2.8ms -> kernel B (attention) 1.9ms -> idle 0.5ms
Stream 1: H2D memcpy pinned-host 14.6ms blocking
CPU: heavy scheduler gaps around memcpy start (~6-18ms window)
```
raj: interesting — memcpy is on stream 1 but it appears to serialize other streams in the capture. suspect host scheduling or a blocking hostcopy path (not cudaMemcpyAsync pinned correctly).
elaine: are we using cudaMemcpy (sync) anywhere in the runtime? batcher used to occasionally fall back to sync copies when pinned pool exhausted.
mike: runtime config shows pinned_pool_max=32, but stress test had ~40 concurrent prefetches. stack fell back to cudaMemcpy (sync) in ~30% of cases — the logs show "hostcopy_fallback: sync" entries.
sara: that explains the 14ms spikes. sync copies block the host thread which then prevents the prefetcher thread from submitting subsequent async copies, so kernels get delayed.
raj: workaround ideas: increase pinned_pool_max, or make fallback spin up a background worker thread that does the sync copy off the main submit path. Also we could throttle prefetch concurrency to stay under pinned pool cap.
elaine: longer-term fix: prefer cudaHostAlloc + cudaMemcpyAsync and a pinned-pool refill strategy. Also check kernel selection — bigger kernels might be more sensitive to these stalls.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: kv_prefetch latency p95 increased from 3.4ms -> 9.8ms after deploy 2024-11-02 (commit 58f3c7).
mike: reproduced locally with synthetic trace: when pinned pool exhausted, p50 ~3ms p95 ~18ms. attaching nsys command used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,cudnn --capture-range=process:launch --output=tmp/trace`
sara: notable in timeline: CPU scheduling gaps exactly line up with worker thread calling blocking memcpy and then getting preempted by other work. Suggest increasing worker thread priority for prefetcher.
raj: low-risk change: make fallback copy use a dedicated io-thread pinned to cpu core and set SCHED_FIFO briefly while copying. can we try that on a canary?
elaine: also evaluate batching heuristic: current microbatch size 16 causes more frequent prefetches. bumping to 24 reduces prefetch rate and amortizes hostcopy cost, but might hurt concurrency for small requests. need perf/quality tradeoff test.
mike: action items: (1) create issue with nsys export + logs (I will), (2) run a canary with pinned_pool_max=64 + io-thread fallback, (3) run microbatch sweep 12/16/24 with load generator and capture nsys timelines for each.
sara: ack. mike, add exact repro script and the command line for the loadgen so we can reproduce in CI.
mike: will do. quick note: avoid cudaDeviceSynchronize in warmup path — I saw an accidental sync introduced in commit 58f3c7 in ringbuffer refactor. removing that alone dropped p95 from 12ms -> 5.1ms in my local run.
raj: good catch. if removing that gets us most of the wins we can roll a patch asap.
elaine: I'll review the ringbuffer PR and file a revert/proper fix.
perf-bot: next steps scheduled: perf-ci will run nsys-based regression job on this branch. results expected in ~2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mike: thanks all. I'll upload the trace export + minimal repro to the issue now. :eyes:
